title_en: People's Procuratorate of Jinshui District, Zhengzhou City, Henan Province v. Yang Zhicheng — theft
ruling_gist_en: According to Article 271 of the Criminal Law of the PRC concerning the crime of embezzlement, the so-called 'taking advantage of one's position' means that the actor, when committing the crime, utilizes his or her own authority, or utilizes the convenience conditions of supervising, managing, or handling the property of the unit that he or she obtains due to the performance of his or her duties. 'Supervision' herein refers to the actor's power to allocate and dispose of the property of the unit within a certain scope; 'management' refers to the actor's duty to directly keep, handle, or use the property of the unit, i.e., having a certain power of disposal over the unit's property; 'handling' refers to the actor's actual control over the unit's property at a specific time and space due to work needs, although not having the duty of supervision or management. Therefore, to constitute the crime of embezzlement, it necessarily requires that when the actor illegally possesses the property of the unit, he or she relies on the authority and responsibilities within his or her position, and uses his or her duties of supervision, management, or handling of the unit's property to carry out the illegal possession while actually controlling, disposing of, or handling the unit's property. If the actor merely has easy access to the unit's property supervised, managed, or handled by others due to his or her work, or is familiar with the crime scene, and uses the convenience conditions formed in the above work to secretly steal the unit's property, then this does not constitute 'taking advantage of one's position', and should be convicted and punished as theft according to Article 264 of the Criminal Law of the PRC.

full_text_en:
**Procuratorate of Jinshui District, Zhengzhou City, Henan Province v. Yang Zhicheng — theft case**

**【Ruling Summary】**

According to the provisions of Article 271 of the Criminal Law of the PRC regarding the crime of embezzlement by taking advantage of one's position, the so-called "taking advantage of one's position" means that when committing a crime, the perpetrator utilizes his own official powers, or takes advantage of the convenience conditions he has obtained due to the execution of his duties in being in charge of, managing, or handling the property of the unit. The term "being in charge" (主管) refers to the perpetrator having the power to allocate and dispose of the property of the unit within a certain scope; the term "managing" (管理) refers to the perpetrator directly having the responsibility to keep, handle, or use the property of the unit, that is, having a certain right to dispose of the property of the unit; the term "handling" (经手) refers to the perpetrator, although not having the duty to be in charge of or manage the property of the unit, actually controlling the property of the unit at a specific time and place due to work needs. Therefore, to constitute the crime of embezzlement by taking advantage of one's position, it is necessarily required that when illegally appropriating the property of the unit, the perpetrator acts based on the authority and duties within his own job scope, utilizes his responsibilities of being in charge of, managing, or handling the property of the unit to a certain extent, and carries out the act of illegal appropriation when actually directing, controlling, or disposing of the property of the unit. If the perpetrator merely has easy access, due to his work, to the property of the unit that is in the charge, management, or handling of others, or is familiar with the crime scene, and uses such convenience conditions formed in the course of work to secretly steal the property of the unit, this does not constitute "taking advantage of one's position" and shall be convicted and punished as the crime of theft in accordance with Article 264 of the Criminal Law of the PRC.

**Procuratorial Authority:** Procuratorate of Jinshui District, Zhengzhou City, Henan Province.

**Defendant:** Yang Zhicheng, male, 29 years old, former computer operator at No. 2 Hall, Renmin Road Store of Zhengzhou Dennis Co., Ltd., residing at Sunbazhai East First Street, Hanghai Road, Zhengzhou City. Arrested on May 19, 2007 in connection with this case.

The Procuratorate of Jinshui District, Zhengzhou City, Henan Province filed a public prosecution with the People's Court of Jinshui District, Zhengzhou City, Henan Province, charging the defendant Yang Zhicheng with theft.

The indictment alleged: Starting from October 2006, the defendant Yang Zhicheng, by means of cracking the program software, entered the VIP points card recharge system of Zhengzhou Dennis Co., Ltd., activated and recharged cancelled VIP points cards, and then used them for personal consumption, totaling RMB 85,000. Yang Zhicheng's conduct has already constituted the crime of theft. It is requested that he be punished according to law.

The defendant Yang Zhicheng and his defense counsel argued: The indictment's allegation that Yang Zhicheng activated and recharged cancelled VIP points cards of Zhengzhou Dennis Co., Ltd. and then used them for personal consumption amounting to RMB 85,000 is inaccurate; the amount should not exceed RMB 50,000. Before the incident, Yang Zhicheng was a computer operator at No. 2 Hall, Renmin Road Store of Zhengzhou Dennis Co., Ltd., and he used the job-related convenience of managing the unit's computers to commit the alleged acts; therefore, the crime should be determined as embezzlement by taking advantage of one's position, not theft. Yang Zhicheng voluntarily surrendered, had a good attitude of admitting guilt after the crime, and showed signs of repentance. It is requested that he be given a lighter punishment according to law.

**Facts Found by the People's Court of Jinshui District, Zhengzhou City at First Instance:**

The VIP points card system program is an internal program of Zhengzhou Dennis Co., Ltd. When a customer purchases a VIP points card from the Group Purchase Department of Zhengzhou Dennis Co., Ltd., the Group Purchase Department applies to the company's Finance Department, and the Finance Department recharges a blank VIP points card and then issues it to the customer.

The defendant Yang Zhicheng was originally a computer operator at No. 2 Hall, Renmin Road Store of Zhengzhou Dennis Co., Ltd., primarily responsible for computer maintenance, cash register maintenance, and the maintenance of the purchase, sales, and inventory system. The computer room where Yang Zhicheng worked was affiliated with the Information Research and Development Center of Zhengzhou Dennis Co., Ltd. As a department responsible for the research and development of the VIP points card system program of Zhengzhou Dennis Co., Ltd., employees of this center and its subordinate computer halls had opportunities to access the VIP points card system program. However, according to company regulations, they were not allowed to crack passwords privately to enter the program, nor did they have the authority to manage or control the company's property.

Starting from October 2006, the defendant Yang Zhicheng, using the work convenience of managing and maintaining the company's computers, cracked the program software, entered the VIP points card recharge system of Zhengzhou Dennis Co., Ltd., activated and recharged cancelled VIP points cards, and then used them for personal consumption. The total consumption amount was RMB 85,000. After the incident, he returned stolen goods and money totaling over RMB 110,000 to Zhengzhou Dennis Co., Ltd.

The above facts are confirmed by the following evidence: the confession of the defendant Yang Zhicheng; the statement of Wu Yongsheng, an employee of Zhengzhou Dennis Co., Ltd.; the testimonies of witnesses Deng Hang, Li Peng, and Kang Feng; the record of case acceptance; the extraction record; photos of the stolen goods; the household registration certificate of Yang Zhicheng and the explanation of his arrest; the detailed list of involved VIP points cards and overdraft consumption; the certificate issued by Zhengzhou Dennis Co., Ltd., the job responsibility description of the company's computer room, and related situation explanations; and the labor contract signed between Yang Zhicheng and Zhengzhou Dennis Co., Ltd., among others, which are sufficient for confirmation.

**Focus of Dispute:** Whether the conduct of the defendant Yang Zhicheng constitutes the crime of theft or the crime of embezzlement by taking advantage of one's position.

**Opinion of the People's Court of Jinshui District, Zhengzhou City at First Instance:**

The defendant Yang Zhicheng was originally a computer operator at No. 2 Hall, Renmin Road Store of Zhengzhou Dennis Co., Ltd., responsible for maintaining the company's computers. He did not have the duty to manage the VIP points card recharge system of Zhengzhou Dennis Co., Ltd. Yang Zhicheng, by cracking the VIP points card system program software, entered the VIP points card recharge system of Zhengzhou Dennis Co., Ltd., activated and recharged cancelled VIP points cards, and then used them for personal consumption. His conduct constitutes the act of secretly stealing the property of others for the purpose of illegal possession. The amount of theft is particularly huge, and the crime of theft is established. The charges brought by the procuratorial authority are established. The defense arguments of Yang Zhicheng and his defense counsel that Yang Zhicheng's conduct constitutes the crime of embezzlement by taking advantage of one's position rather than the crime of theft are not established and are not adopted. Yang Zhicheng's defense argument that the amount of theft is less than RMB 50,000 is inconsistent with the facts and evidence found at trial and is not supported. The defense counsel argued that Yang Zhicheng voluntarily surrendered and should be given a lighter or mitigated punishment according to law. Upon investigation, Yang Zhicheng admitted his criminal facts only after Zhengzhou Dennis Co., Ltd. discovered his use of the reactivated and recharged VIP points cards for personal consumption and questioned him about the situation. This does not meet the constitutive elements of voluntary surrender. Therefore, the above defense opinion of the defense counsel is not supported. After Yang Zhicheng was brought to justice, he showed a relatively good attitude of admitting guilt and signs of repentance. This can be considered in giving a lighter punishment at the court's discretion. The defense opinion of the defense counsel that Yang Zhicheng had a good attitude of admitting guilt and showed signs of repentance, suggesting a lighter punishment, is established and adopted.

Accordingly, the People's Court of Jinshui District, Zhengzhou City, in accordance with Article 264 of the Criminal Law of the PRC (hereinafter referred to as the Criminal Law), on November 27, 2007, rendered the following judgment:

The defendant Yang Zhicheng is convicted of theft and sentenced to ten years' imprisonment and a fine of RMB 10,000.

Yang Zhicheng refused to accept the judgment of first instance and appealed to the Intermediate People's Court of Zhengzhou City. His main grounds of appeal were: The computer room staff of Zhengzhou Dennis Co., Ltd., including the appellant, all had the right to enter the company's VIP points card recharge system. The appellant committed the alleged criminal acts by taking advantage of his position. Therefore, the appellant's conduct does not constitute the crime of theft and should be convicted and punished as the crime of embezzlement by taking advantage of one's position. The first instance judgment erred in its characterization. It is requested that the second instance modify the judgment according to law.

After the second instance trial, the Intermediate People's Court of Zhengzhou City confirmed the facts found in the first instance.

The focus of dispute in the second instance remained whether the conduct of the appellant Yang Zhicheng constituted the crime of theft or the crime of embezzlement by taking advantage of one's position.

**Opinion of the Intermediate People's Court of Zhengzhou City at Second Instance:**

According to Article 264 of the Criminal Law, the crime of theft refers to the act of secretly stealing relatively large amounts of public or private property for the purpose of illegal possession. According to Article 271 of the Criminal Law, the crime of embezzlement by taking advantage of one's position refers to an employee of a company, enterprise, or other unit who, taking advantage of his position, illegally appropriates property of the unit in relatively large amounts.

Both the crime of theft and the crime of embezzlement by taking advantage of one's position are types of property crimes stipulated in Chapter Five of the Criminal Law. Their commonality lies in that the perpetrator subjectively harbors the criminal purpose of illegally possessing public or private property, and both infringe upon the legitimate rights of public or private property. Their differences are: First, the subject of the crime of embezzlement by taking advantage of one's position is a special subject, i.e., only employees of a company, enterprise, or other unit. The subject of theft is a general subject who has reached the age of criminal responsibility and has criminal responsibility capacity. Second, the crime of embezzlement by taking advantage of one's position is objectively manifested as taking advantage of one's position to illegally appropriate property of the unit in relatively large amounts. The specific methods of illegal appropriation are diverse, including theft, fraud, direct misappropriation, etc. The crime of theft is objectively manifested as secretly stealing public or private property. Third, the object of the crime of embezzlement by taking advantage of one's position is the property of the unit where the perpetrator works, while the object of theft is unspecified public or private property.

To determine whether the conduct of the appellant Yang Zhicheng constitutes the crime of theft or the crime of embezzlement by taking advantage of one's position, the key lies in analyzing whether Yang Zhicheng took advantage of his job-related convenience when committing the alleged criminal acts.

According to the provisions of Article 271 of the Criminal Law regarding the crime of embezzlement by taking advantage of one's position, the so-called "taking advantage of one's position" means that when committing a crime, the perpetrator utilizes his own official powers, or takes advantage of the convenience conditions he has obtained due to the execution of his duties in being in charge of, managing, or handling the property of the unit. The term "being in charge" refers to the perpetrator having the power to allocate and dispose of the property of the unit within a certain scope; the term "managing" refers to the perpetrator directly having the responsibility to keep, handle, or use the property of the unit, that is, having a certain right to dispose of the property of the unit; the term "handling" refers to the perpetrator, although not having the duty to be in charge of or manage the property of the unit, actually controlling the property of the unit at a specific time and place due to work needs. Therefore, to constitute the crime of embezzlement by taking advantage of one's position, it is necessarily required that when illegally appropriating the property of the unit, the perpetrator acts based on the authority and duties within his own job scope, utilizes his responsibilities of being in charge of, managing, or handling the property of the unit to a certain extent, and carries out the act of illegal appropriation when actually directing, controlling, or disposing of the property of the unit. If the perpetrator merely has easy access, due to his work, to the property of the unit that is in the charge, management, or handling of others, or is familiar with the crime scene, and uses such convenience conditions formed in the course of work to secretly steal the property of the unit, this does not constitute "taking advantage of one's position" and shall be convicted and punished as the crime of theft in accordance with Article 264 of the Criminal Law. In this case, when the appellant Yang Zhicheng committed the alleged acts and illegally appropriated the property of the unit, although to some extent he did utilize the work convenience of being a computer room staff member of Zhengzhou Dennis Co., Ltd. and having easy access to the company's computers, he neither had the responsibility of being in charge of, managing, or handling the property of the unit, nor did he have the responsibility of managing the unit's VIP points card recharge system, nor did he possess the program password for the VIP points card recharge system. The ultimate realization of his criminal purpose of illegally appropriating the unit's property was achieved by committing the secret theft act, not by taking advantage of his own position.

First, the issuance procedure of the VIP points cards of Zhengzhou Dennis Co., Ltd. determines that the appellant Yang Zhicheng did not have the convenience conditions of his position when committing the alleged criminal acts. Customers purchasing VIP points cards of Zhengzhou Dennis Co., Ltd. must buy them from the company's Group Purchase Department, which then applies to the company's Finance Department, and finally the Finance Department recharges blank VIP points cards and issues them to customers. It can be seen that as a computer operator at No. 2 Hall, Renmin Road Store, the appellant simply had no responsibility of being in charge of, handling, or managing the property of Zhengzhou Dennis Co., Ltd., and naturally there was no basis for taking advantage of his position to commit the alleged criminal acts.

Second, the job duties of the appellant Yang Zhicheng were primarily responsible for maintaining the computers, cash registers, and the purchase, sales, and inventory system at No. 2 Hall, Renmin Road Store of Zhengzhou Dennis Co., Ltd. The computer room where Yang Zhicheng worked was affiliated with the Information Research and Development Center of Zhengzhou Dennis Co., Ltd. As a department responsible for the research and development of the VIP points card system program of Zhengzhou Dennis Co., Ltd., although employees of this center and its subordinate computer halls had opportunities to access the VIP points card system program, they did not have the duty to manage or control the system, and according to company regulations, they were not allowed to crack the password privately to enter the program. It can be seen that when committing the alleged criminal acts, the appellant only utilized his "work convenience" of being a computer management employee with easy access to the company's computers, but this "work convenience" could not directly lead to the appellant illegally appropriating the unit's property.

Third, according to the facts of this case, the appellant Yang Zhicheng, driven by the purpose of illegal possession, violated the unit's regulations, privately cracked the password to enter the unit's VIP points card recharge management system program, then activated and recharged cancelled VIP points cards and used them for personal consumption. Therefore, the appellant did not enter the unit's VIP points card recharge management system program by taking advantage of his own position, but instead used his expertise in computer technology to illegally crack the password to intrude into the system program and then commit the alleged criminal acts. His conduct constitutes secret theft and should be convicted and punished as the crime of theft.

Accordingly, the Intermediate People's Court of Zhengzhou City held that the original judgment's determination that the appellant Yang Zhicheng committed the crime of theft had clear facts, reliable and sufficient evidence, accurate conviction, appropriate sentencing, and legal trial procedures. The appellant Yang Zhicheng's grounds of appeal were all unfounded and were not adopted. In accordance with Item (1) of Article 189 of the Criminal Procedure Law of the PRC, the court ruled on March 19, 2008, as follows:

The appeal is dismissed, and the original judgment is affirmed.

This ruling is final.
